newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn sees EMU speculation unsettling markets.
newsitem.headline: Bonn sees EMU speculation unsettling markets.

text.p: Speculation about delaying Europe's single currency was unsettling Germany's economy as well as currency and financial markets, a conservative German parliamentary leader said on Wednesday.

"The on-going speculation about the introduction of the euro is unsettling not only the finance and currency markets but also the economy," said Friedhelm Ost, a top parliiamentary lieutenant in Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democratic (CDU) party.
Instead of speculating about the start of European economic and monetary union (EMU), it would be better to work toward strengthening the economy for more growth and jobs, he said.

"A strong rise of gross domestic product especially would help Germany meet the convergence criteria," he said. "Despite all the claims of euro-opponents to the contrary, Germany has a good chance to qualify for the European currency union."
Ost also said Bonn's tax reforms and social security cutbacks would improve conditions for jobs and growth.
